title: O Happy Is the Man, Who Hears
description: O Happy Is the Man, Who Hears in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: John Logan wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 404 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Wisdom”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O hap-py is the man, who hears In-struc-tion's warn-ing voice; And who ce-les-tial wis-dom makes His ear-ly, on-ly choice.

lines: O happy is the man, who hears
Her treasures are of more esteem
And her rewards more precious are
Than all their mines of gold.
In her right hand she holds to view
She guides the young with innocence
A crown of glory she bestows
Her ways are ways of pleasantness,
And all her paths are peace.

licence: Public domain: John Logan died in 1788.
credits: Words by John Logan (1748–1788), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
